Design workflow · Source reviewed 2026-11-22

A distinctive design, grounded in your Figma file.

Combine Anthropic’s Frontend Design skill with Figma’s official plugin: a direction for the visual work, and a connection to the design you actually own.

Choose your starting point

Start with Frontend Design when your brief leaves room to explore. Add Figma when you have an approved frame to implement.

A skill supplies instructions. A plugin bundles capabilities; Figma’s includes an MCP connection and its own skills. MCP gives the agent access to tools and data. Neither automatically makes an interface usable.

Before you start

This route uses Claude Code, a local website project and an account with Claude Code access. If you are new to terminals, follow the official quickstart first. You also need a Figma account with access to the target file. The remote connection does not require Figma’s desktop app.

Claude Code needs eligible paid or API access. Figma read limits depend on plan and seat: Starter, View and Collab access currently allow up to 20 reads per month. Check the linked limits before a large task; some image-generation actions consume separate credits.

1. Add design guidance

Inside a Claude Code conversation in a copy of your website project, run:

/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills

This installs the example collection, which includes Frontend Design. Confirm it in the plugin manager, then request the skill by name.

2. Connect the official Figma plugin

In your terminal, run the command from Figma’s setup page:

claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official

Restart Claude Code. Open /plugin, go to Installed, select Figma, and follow the browser sign-in. Review access before allowing it. Return to the plugin manager and confirm connected status. If your organisation blocks it, follow its policy and Figma’s manual setup instructions.

3. Give the design a real subject

Paste your own frame link into this starter brief.

Use Frontend Design and the official Figma tools.
Subject: a local ceramics studio offering one beginner workshop.
Audience: adults choosing their first hands-on class.
Primary action: view available workshop dates.
Use this approved Figma frame: [paste the frame link].
First inspect the frame and identify the existing typography, spacing and components.
Propose one visual direction grounded in clay, tools and the workshop setting.
Explain any departure from the approved frame before implementing it.
Build only the workshop page in this project. Keep dates and prices as supplied; mark missing facts.
Check mobile layout, keyboard focus and reduced motion. Do not publish.

If you have no approved frame, skip the Figma connection and start from the brief. If you have a strict design system, ask the agent to preserve it; expressive guidance must not override your approved constraints.

4. Review before keeping it

  • Ask which frame and components were read. A connection badge alone does not prove the correct file was used.
  • Compare the rendered page with the chosen frame at desktop and narrow mobile widths.
  • Reach the primary action using only the keyboard; inspect visible focus and meaningful button text.
  • Check real dates, prices, image rights and font availability yourself.

If access fails, check the signed-in account, frame URL and file permissions. If the result drifts, reduce the task to one frame and list the elements that must match. Disable the plugin in the manager when you no longer need it; disconnect account access through the provider when appropriate. Keep your project copy until you approve the diff.
